subject: Designing deterministic health tooling for skill libraries, including source/schema inventory, protocol/projection…

evals.prompt: Define skill-infrastructure in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the skill-infrastructure skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind skill-infrastructure. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "scaffold a new SKILL.md for our team''s deploy procedure". Should skill-infrastructure activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force skill-infrastructure onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to lint-overlay, skill-scaffold, graph-audit, testing-strategy, project-knowledge-extraction, code-review.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "our skill library is growing and we''re getting silent decay — eval counts dropping, conflicts emerging — what tooling should we add?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying skill-infrastructure.

Place skill-infrastructure among its adjacent skills (lint-overlay, skill-scaffold, graph-audit, testing-strategy, project-knowledge-extraction, code-review). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about skill-infrastructure and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
